overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the central concepts of Merleau-Ponty's late ontology. You'll be asked about flesh as element, reversibility and its gap, the chiasm, the seer's visibility, and the invisible of the visible.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

options.html: Because it's the smallest particle of matter
options.text: Because it's the smallest particle of matter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Flesh isn't matter. "Element" names a general manner of being.

options.html: Because it's a general way of being, like water
options.text: Because it's a general way of being, like water
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An element in the old sense lies between the individual thing and the idea.

options.html: Because it's a basic idea in the mind
options.text: Because it's a basic idea in the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Flesh isn't mind. It's a general way of being shared by body and world.

options.html: Because it's the chemical makeup of the body
options.text: Because it's the chemical makeup of the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Flesh isn't the body's tissue. It's a general way of being.

forms.stemHtml: When your left hand touches your right hand as it touches a table, what does Merleau-Ponty say about the two roles?

options.html: They coincide, so you feel both at once
options.text: They coincide, so you feel both at once
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The roles reverse but never coincide.

options.html: Only the left hand ever touches
options.text: Only the left hand ever touches
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The right hand can also be felt as touching. The roles can reverse.
Correct! The reversal is always imminent and never complete.
Sorry, that's incorrect. They're related by reversibility: each role can pass into the other.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are true of divergence (écart) in Merleau-Ponty's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It keeps perceiver and perceived distinct
options.text: It keeps perceiver and perceived distinct
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Without it, there would be no one perceiving anything.

options.html: It's structural, not a failure of perception
options.text: It's structural, not a failure of perception
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The gap makes perception possible.
Correct! It's why the reversal is never complete.

options.html: It's empty space between two separate substances
options.text: It's empty space between two separate substances
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's a difference within one flesh, like a fold in cloth.

options.html: It can be overcome by closer attention
options.text: It can be overcome by closer attention
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's structural and can't be overcome.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term, from the Greek letter for a crossing, for the exchange between perceiver and perceived in which each passes into the other without merging? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty also calls it the intertwining.
Correct! Merleau-Ponty also calls it the intertwining.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty calls this the chiasm.

forms.stemHtml: What does Merleau-Ponty mean by "the invisible of the visible"?

options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Hidden objects are visible in principle. The invisible belongs to the visible as its depth and meaning.

options.html: A realm of pure ideas separate from the senses
options.text: A realm of pure ideas separate from the senses
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The invisible isn't separate. It belongs to this visible world.

options.html: The depth, structure, and meaning the visible carries
options.text: The depth, structure, and meaning the visible carries
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Like a musical idea that exists only through its sounds.

options.html: Whatever falls outside the range of human eyes
options.text: Whatever falls outside the range of human eyes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The invisible isn't a limit of vision. It's the depth and meaning of the visible.

title: Flesh, Reversibility, Chiasm
